characterization_methods: Scanning Electron Microscopy with Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (SEM-EDS)
evidence: Grazing incident angle X-ray diffraction (GIAXRD, PANalytical X’Pert PRO MRD, incident angel: ∼3°) was performed to find out crystallinity and the corresponding phases of the as-grown and annealed MoN x films. The composition in the film was investigated by secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS, CAMECA IMS-6f) using 1.5 keV Cs + beam. The elemental presence and their oxidation states were found out from X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, ESCALAB 250 spectrometer). The scanning electron microscopy with the energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM -EDS, Hitachi, S -4800) and the cross-sectional view transmission electron microscopy (TEM, Hitachi, HF-3300) were adopted for detailed understanding of the MoN x@NF composite. The Nyquist plot obtained from the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements carried out in a frequency range of 0. 1 Hz to 100 kHz as shown in figure 3d . The cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements of the ALD-MoNx@NF composite electrode were carried out within a favorable potential window of -0.1 to 0.5 V in 1M aqueous KOH solution. The post-cycling SEM image (inset , Figure 3d ) clearly shows the considerable surface roughing and agglomeration of the active material.
